why: Cross-reader rows for the owner record of the test-leftovers contract (.agents/conventions/common/test-leftovers.md §3):
<owner>:<host>@<os>:<pid>[:<start>[:<ns>]] with <os> one of linux, macos, windows. COAI-OWNED; E5 S3 (plan row 15). The C# reader
(Owner.Parse) and the Node reader (parseOwner, parseLegacyOwner of .agents/conventions/tools/lib/owned.mjs) are asked about every row,
and the live claim of the running test folder is one more row. OldAndNewClaims_AreReadByBothReaders is the test.
csharp / node: 'owner' = the reader returns an owner, 'unreadable' = it returns none. nodeOldForm: 'legacy' = parseLegacyOwner reads it
(only the old <host>@linux:<pid>:<start> shape, the one old-grammar spelling the Node sweeper still judges), else 'unreadable'.
The old spellings (win32, darwin, no owner segment) are unreadable to BOTH new readers: a run that wrote one would be kept for ever.
